James Montgomery
JAYMZ munt-GUM-er-ee
proper noun
English form of the Hebrew Jacob through Greek and Latin (James), joined to the Norman-French place-name surname Montgomery (“Gomeric’s hill”); the name of the Sheffield editor and hymnwriter.

See also: James Montgomery

📖 Biblical Definition

James Montgomery (1771–1854), son of Moravian missionaries who died on the mission field of the West Indies, was reared among the Brethren and, though he wandered for a season, was recovered to a warm and steadfast evangelical faith. He became editor of a Sheffield newspaper and was twice imprisoned for the boldness of his convictions, yet he bore the reproach patiently and used his pen for righteousness. Of his some four hundred hymns, two stand as jewels of the church. “Angels from the Realms of Glory” gathers shepherds, sages, and saints to worship the incarnate Son—“come and worship, worship Christ, the newborn King”—setting the whole created order in adoration before the manger. “Hail to the Lord’s Anointed” is a majestic versification of Psalm 72, hymning the reign of the promised King whose “kingdom still increasing, a kingdom without end,” shall break oppression, bless the poor, and stretch from sea to sea. Montgomery also gave the church its finest hymn on prayer, “Prayer is the soul’s sincere desire.” A layman singing amid the world’s traffic, twice jailed yet unbroken, he is honored as a hymnist who wedded the loftiness of the Psalms to the sure hope of Christ’s advancing kingdom.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

English editor and hymnwriter (1771–1854), author of “Angels from the Realms of Glory” and “Hail to the Lord’s Anointed.”

JAMES MONTGOMERY, proper noun. Scottish-born English poet, newspaper editor, and hymnwriter (1771–1854).

Son of Moravian missionaries who died abroad in the West Indies; reared among the Brethren.

Editor at Sheffield, twice imprisoned for his outspoken convictions, yet unbroken in faith.

Author of some four hundred hymns, including a beloved versification of Psalm 72.

Chiefly remembered for “Angels from the Realms of Glory,” “Hail to the Lord’s Anointed,” and “Prayer Is the Soul’s Sincere Desire.”

📖 Key Scripture

Psa 72:8 — "He shall have dominion also from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth."

Psa 72:11 — "Yea, all kings shall fall down before him: all nations shall serve him."

Luk 2:13 — "And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host praising God, and saying,"

Isa 61:1 — "The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound;"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A faithful witness, not a contested doctrine; his life recovers the hope of Messiah’s advancing kingdom.

expand to see more

This entry is preserved to honor a layman who used the editor’s desk and the poet’s pen for the kingdom of Christ, and who bore imprisonment for conscience without bitterness. It is an example, not a doctrine to be defended against distortion.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the reign of Christ, the Lord’s Anointed, whose kingdom truly advances in the earth. “He comes with succour speedy to those who suffer wrong; to help the poor and needy, and bid the weak be strong.” Let the church sing Psalm 72 with confidence that the Son shall have dominion from sea to sea, and let this hope stir her to worship and to mission.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The name of a jailed editor who sang the manger and the throne of the Anointed King.

expand to see more

James — the English form of Jacob, “supplanter,” borne by apostles and kings alike.

Montgomery — a Norman place-name surname, “Gomeric’s hill,” carried into Britain by conquest.

The Moravian missionary heritage of his parents stamped his verse with a global, gospel-spreading vision.

Psalm 72 supplies the royal frame of “Hail to the Lord’s Anointed,” a hymn of Messiah’s reign.

The angelic host of Luke 2 opens “Angels from the Realms of Glory,” summoning all to worship the newborn King.

Usage

"“Montgomery was twice in prison, yet his hymns crown Christ as King.”"

"“At Advent we sing ‘Angels from the Realms of Glory’ and call all creation to worship.”"

"“‘Hail to the Lord’s Anointed’ is Psalm 72 made a coronation song.”"
